rules.title: Game Overview
rules: A standard game is played by two players. The Comprehensive Rules do not currently support games played by more than two players.
The game concludes when a player loses. The player who didn't lose is considered the winner.
If a player's leader's defense is 0 or less, that player is considered to have fulfilled a loss condition.
If a player must draw a card when there are no cards remaining in their deck, that player is considered to have fulfilled a loss condition.
If all players lose simultaneously, the game ends in a draw.
Players may concede at any point during the game. When a player concedes, they lose the game immediately, and the game concludes; Confirmation Timing (10.5) does not occur.
The act of conceding is not affected by any card. A card effect cannot force a player to concede, nor can a replacement effect replace a loss resulting from concession.

A card may produce an effect that causes a player to win or lose the game. In such cases, the player wins or loses immediately when the effect is processed, and the game concludes; Confirmation Timing (10.5) does not occur.
If card text should ever be contradicted by the Comprehensive Rules, the card text takes precedence.

If a player is required to perform an impossible action for any reason, the action is not performed. Similarly, if an effect requires a player to perform multiple actions, part of which cannot be performed, the player performs as many actions as possible.
If required to put something into a state that it is already in, that action is not performed.

If, for any reason, an action is to be performed zero or a negative number of times, or if an action would be based on zero or a negative value (aside from adding, subtracting, or comparing), the action is not performed at all. A negative value never indicates an opposite action.
If instructed to deal 0 damage, that instance of damage does not happen at all. (Damage is not considered to have been dealt.)
If it becomes necessary to perform an action that would be based on a negative value (aside from adding, subtracting), treat the value as zero.
An effect has reduced the cost of a card to a negative value. That card would be played for zero play points.

If multiple effects that require a player to perform a certain action are produced simultaneously, and it is not possible to perform all of them, the player is required to select and perform as many of the actions as possible.
Numeric information possessed by players or cards can be zero or a negative value, unless an upper or lower limit is specified.
When a certain value would rise above or fall below an upper or lower limit, it instead becomes the value specified by the limit.
If a card's effect instructs a player to perform an action that is prohibited by another active effect, the prohibiting effect takes precedence.

In the case that multiple players are required to make a selection simultaneously while processing effects, if it is before the game, players make their selections in turn order. If it is during the game, the active player selects first. The non-active player makes their selection after the active player makes their selection known to them.

If a certain effect applies to multiple players, and that effect requires executing multiple processes, each process that does not involve selection is executed simultaneously, while each process that does involve selection is executed starting with the active player.

An effect reads, "Each player draws a card. Each player may put a follower from their hand onto the field." This effect is handled in the following order: (1) Both players draw a card. (2) The active player may put a follower from their hand onto the field. (3) The nonactive player may put a follower from their hand onto the field.

When a player is required by a card or a rule to select a number, the player must select an integer equal to or greater than zero, unless indicated otherwise. Fractions less than one and negative numbers may not be selected.
If a card or rule specifies a numerical limit (e.g., "up to X"), the player may choose zero as long as a minimum value isn't specified.
If reference is made to information that a card does not possess, the following rules apply.
When counting the number of cards in a group which possess that information or different values of that information, the card in question does not count.
A condition which depends on the comparison of that information to some other information is never satisfied.
A condition which depends on the comparison of that information to some other information is never satisfied.

rules: Card Information Follower Evolved Follower Collaboration Follower Universe Card Spell Amulet
This is the card's unique name.

Whenever a rule or card text contains "[card name]" (a name written in bold and italics), it refers to any card with the same name or, depending on the context, any card whose name contains that name. In reminder text or other contexts where the surrounding text is italicized, the card name may be unitalicized as a result of reverse- ① Card Name ② Class ③ Card Type ④ Trait ⑤ Cost ⑥ Card Text ⑦ Attack ⑧ Defense ⑨ Token Information ⑩ Card Art ⑪ Rarity ⑫ Miscellaneous ⑬ Alternate Name ⑭ Universe Leader italicization.
An alternate name (2.13) cannot be referred to in this way unless referred to in its entirety.
This indicates the class to which the card belongs.
Classes are represented by icons: Neutral Forestcraft Swordcraft Runecraft
This provides information about tokens referred to by the card's effect(s).
This information is provided for players' reference; it does not have any significance in regard to the rules.
Card art has no bearing on gameplay. Dragoncraft Abysscraft Havencraft
Class information affects deck construction and is referred to by some card abilities.
The primary card types are "leader," "follower," "amulet," "spell," and "crest."
Some cards have a special type.
Special types include "evolved" cards and "advanced" cards.
Whenever a rule, ability, or effect refers to only a card type, it refers to all cards of that type.
Traits don't have any significance in regard to the rules, but other cards may refer to them.
This indicates the amount of play points that the player must pay to play the card (10.4.3). Whenever a card refers to a "cost," it is referring to this displayed number.
This indicates the card's unique abilities, effects, and other information.

Sentences that are enclosed in parentheses are called "explanatory text" or "reminder text." Although these are a part of a card's text, their only purpose is to clarify how an ability works; they serve no other game function.
This signifies the base amount of damage the card deals when it attacks.
Attack is represented by the icon in card text.
This signifies the amount of damage the card must take before it is destroyed.
Defense is represented by the icon in card text.
Whenever a follower or leader takes damage, that card's defense is reduced by the same amount of damage (5.14.1).
Although not indicated on leader cards, leaders also have defense.
Unless otherwise indicated, a leader's defense is 20.
Rarity has no bearing on gameplay.
This part of the card contains miscellaneous information such as collector numbers and copyright information, as well as universe information.
Aside from the following exceptions, this information has no bearing on gameplay.
Universe information can affect deck construction.
Collector numbers are used to distinguish between the front and back face of a double-faced card (2.14).
Some cards have an alternate name in addition to their regular card name.
Whenever an ability or effect refers to a card's alternate name in its entirety, it refers to the card name of the card with that alternate name.
A double-faced card is a card that has information on both sides.
The "front face" of a double-faced card is the side with its collector number, while the other side is the "back face."
When in a zone other than the field, evolve zone, or evolve deck area, a double-faced card is treated as having the information of its front face.
When put onto the field or into the evolve zone, a double-faced card should be placed so that the appropriate face, as specified by rules or effects, is visible to all players.
When referencing the information of a double-faced card on the field or in the evolve zone, reference the information of the visible face.

rules.title: Player Information
rules: The "owner" of a card is the player who physically owns the card and started the game with it in their deck. When the game ends, each player returns the cards they own back into their deck.
The "controller" of a card, ability, or effect is the player who is currently using it. The controller of a card put in a given zone is the player to whom that zone belongs.
A passive ability's controller is the player who controls the card with the ability or the effect that produced the ability.
An activated ability's controller is the player who played it.
An automatic ability's controller is the player who controls the card with the ability or the effect that produced the ability.
An effect's controller is the player who controls the ability that produced it.
If an effect requires a player to perform an action without specifying which player, that effect's controller performs the action.
Play Points, Evolution Points, and SuperEvolution Points
"Play points," "maximum play points," and "evolution points" are types of numeric information that each player possesses.
Play points represent the cost that players must pay to perform certain actions, such as playing a card or evolving a follower (10.4.3).
Maximum play points represent the number of play points a player receives at the start of their turn.

There are lower and upper limits to the amount of play points and maximum play points a player can have. If, during a game, a player's play points or maximum play points would rise above or fall beneath these limits, their play points or maximum play points become equal to the respective limit instead.
The lower limit for maximum play points is 0. The upper limit for maximum play points is 10.
The lower limit for play points is 0, while the upper limit is equal to the player's current maximum play points.
Evolution points are represented by "Evolution Point" cards and may be used by a player in lieu of 1 play point when playing an evolve ability (12.2).
The lower limit for evolution points is 0.
Super-evolution points are represented by "Super-Evolution Point" cards and are used by players for super-evolution (12.2.4).
The lower limit for super-evolution points is 0.
"Turns passed" is a type of numeric information that each player possesses.
A player's turns passed is the number of times they have begun their start phase (7.2) as the active player for the first time in a turn.
If a player skips a turn (5.26), that turn does not count towards their turns passed.
If a player takes another turn (5.28), that turn counts towards their turns passed.
